1.s: When was Dholavira inhabited, in seven stages, according to R. S. Bisht?
1.x: Dholavira: inhabited c. 3000–1800 BCE in seven stages (R. S. Bisht); UNESCO: 3rd to mid-2nd millennium BCE.

2.s: What is the single most distinctive feature of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
2.x: Hallmark / specialisation: town planning (urban centres, grid, drains) – the single most distinctive feature of the IVC.

2.s: What material was used in almost all Harappan buildings, unlike the mainly dried bricks of Egypt?
2.x: Most significant feature: burnt-brick buildings – burnt bricks in almost all constructions (Egypt used mainly dried bricks).

2.s: Which two cities is the Indus Valley Civilisation chiefly known for?
2.x: Known for – Town planning; Mohenjodaro and Harappa; agriculture and craft industry (bead, shell, metal factories)

2.s: Which buildings have not clearly been found in Harappan cities, unlike in Mesopotamia and Egypt?
2.x: Public buildings – No temples or palaces clearly found, unlike Mesopotamia and Egypt

2.s: What do standard bricks, grid streets and covered drains in Harappan cities point to?
2.x: Civic authority – Standard bricks, grid, streets and drains point to a civic authority; the absence of palaces or temples does not disprove it

2.s: How many pillars did the assembly hall at Mohenjodaro have?
2.x: Known – Pillars (Mohenjodaro assembly hall, 20 pillars), wells, drains, bows and arrows

2.s: When did iron come into use in India, in the Later Vedic age?
2.x: Unknown – The true arch (only the corbelled arch) and iron – a Bronze Age culture; iron came c. 1000 BC (Later Vedic)

2.s: What kind of script did the Harappans use?
2.x: Script – Pictographic (undeciphered) – No script

2.s: Which were the main metals in Harappan use?
2.x: Metal – Copper, bronze; no iron – Iron in the Later Vedic age

2.s: What kind of pottery is typical of the Harappans?
2.x: Pottery – Red ware painted in black – Painted Grey Ware

2.s: Which pottery is associated with the Vedic culture?
2.x: Pottery – Red ware painted in black – Painted Grey Ware

2.s: Which evidence places the IVC before the Aryans, as its sequence lies below the Painted Grey Ware?
2.x: Pottery places the IVC before the Aryans: the stratified sequence (from Mehrgarh to the black-on-red Harappan ware) lies below the Painted Grey Ware of the Vedic people.

2.s: To which age does the Indus Valley Civilisation, which had no iron, belong?
2.x: The IVC was a Bronze Age culture: no iron.

2.s: Which Harappan city had the most wells, about 700 of brick?
2.x: Mohenjodaro – About 700 brick wells, many inside houses – the most wells

2.s: How many reservoirs formed part of the water system of Dholavira?
2.x: Dholavira – Water management: 16 reservoirs, dams, embankments, channels; some rock-cut

2.s: What kind of drains did houses at Kalibangan have?
2.x: Kalibangan – Many houses had their own wells; wooden drains

2.s: Which Harappan site had no systematic drainage?
2.x: Banawali – No systematic drainage

2.s: Which Harappan site in Sindh is known for well irrigation?
2.x: Allahdino (Sindh) – Well irrigation

2.s: How were the street drains of Harappan cities built?
o: Covered, with bricks or stone slabs
2.x: Drainage = the most advanced IVC feature: house drains → sump / cesspit → covered street drains (bricks or stone slabs) with manholes → soak pits or main channels; streets sloped for flow; better than in contemporary Mesopotamia and Egypt.

2.s: What material was used for the drains at Lothal, where houses were of mud brick?
2.x: Lothal: mud-brick houses but burnt-brick drains.

2.s: Which rivulets fed the reservoirs of Dholavira?
2.x: Water source – The Manhar and Mansar rivulets

2.s: How deep was the largest rock-cut reservoir at Dholavira?
2.x: Largest reservoir – Rock-cut, about 73–79 m long, 7 m deep

2.s: In which rock were the stepwells of Dholavira cut?
2.x: Stepwells – Cut in sandstone = Harappan rock-cut architecture

2.s: Which Harappan city is noted for reservoirs and water harvesting?
2.x: Dholavira = reservoirs (water harvesting); Mohenjodaro = wells.

2.s: On which side of Mohenjodaro and Harappa stood the citadel?
2.x: Mohenjodaro, Harappa – Citadel on the west (smaller, higher, on a mud-brick platform; elite and public buildings) + lower town on the east (larger; commoners)

2.s: Which Harappan city had both its citadel and its lower town fortified?
2.x: Kalibangan – Citadel + lower town, both fortified

2.s: Which is the only Harappan city in three parts: citadel, middle town and lower town?
2.x: Dholavira – Only city in three parts: citadel, middle town, lower town

2.s: Which is the only Harappan city without a citadel?
2.x: Chanhudaro – No citadel (the only Harappan city without one)

2.s: Which two Harappan sites had the citadel inside one fortified enclosure, not separately walled?
2.x: Lothal, Surkotada – Citadel not separately walled; inside one fortified enclosure

2.s: What was the plan of the Harappan site of Sutkagendor?
o: Three parts with a middle town
2.x: Sutkagendor – Citadel + lower city

2.s: On which raised part of Mohenjodaro stood the Great Bath, the granary and the assembly hall?
2.x: The Great Bath, granary, college of priests and assembly hall stood on the western citadel of Mohenjodaro.

2.s: Which of these is a later city, not a Harappan site?
2.x: IVC sites include Kalibangan, Ropar and Lothal; Pataliputra is a later city.

2.s: At which Harappan site were mud bricks used instead of the usual burnt bricks?
2.x: Material – Burnt bricks common; mud bricks for fillings and platforms and at Kalibangan

2.s: What size were Harappan house bricks?
2.x: Sizes – Same ratio, different sizes: house bricks 7.5 × 30 cm, city-wall bricks 10 × 40 cm

2.s: What building material was used at Dholavira instead of baked brick?
2.x: Dholavira – Sandstone and limestone blocks, not baked brick

2.s: At which Harappan site were ornamental bricks found?
2.x: Ornamental bricks – Kalibangan

2.s: Which Harappan site is associated with curved bricks?
2.x: Curved bricks – Chanhudaro

2.s: How did the north–south and east–west streets of Harappan cities cross each other?
2.x: Grid layout – Streets ran north–south and east–west, crossing at right angles and splitting the city into blocks; broad and straight

2.s: How wide were the main streets of Harappan cities?
2.x: Width – Main streets about 10 m (30 feet)

2.s: Which is the only Harappan city with radial streets?
2.x: Banawali – The only city with radial streets

2.s: What were the rooms of a Harappan house arranged round?
2.x: Plan – Rooms round a central courtyard; brick-paved bathrooms and toilets; no ground-level windows (privacy)

2.s: Which Harappan city is the exception, with house entrances on the main street?
2.x: Entrances – On side lanes, not main streets; Lothal is the exception (entrances on the main street)

2.s: What evidence shows that many Harappan houses had an upper storey?
2.x: Storeys – Most houses single-storeyed, but staircases show many had an upper storey

2.s: Which kind of arch did Harappan builders know?
2.x: Arch – Only the corbelled arch, never the true arch

2.s: At which site is the Great Bath?
2.x: Site – Mohenjodaro, on the citadel mound, Sindh

2.s: What are the dimensions of the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro?
2.x: Size – 11.88 × 7.01 m, 2.43 m deep; two flights of steps on the north and south

2.s: What was used to waterproof the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro?
2.x: Material – Burnt bricks set in gypsum mortar; bitumen (natural tar) waterproofing

2.s: What was the water source of the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro?
o: A large well in a side room
2.x: Water – From a large well in a side room; drain in one corner

2.s: What is the common view of the purpose of the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro?
2.x: Purpose – Ritual bath (the common view); a public bath is unlikely as houses had bathrooms

2.s: At which site is the Great Granary, the largest building (45.71 × 15.23 m) on the citadel?
2.x: Great Granary – the largest building (45.71 × 15.23 m), on the citadel – Mohenjodaro

2.s: Where is Granary of 12 rooms in two rows of six, near the Ravi?
2.x: Granary of 12 rooms in two rows of six, near the Ravi – Harappa

2.s: Which sites, besides Mohenjodaro and Harappa, had granaries?
2.x: Other granaries – Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi

2.s: At which site stood a warehouse on a raised platform beside the dock, with seal impressions?
2.x: Warehouse on a raised platform beside the dock; seal impressions – Lothal

2.s: Where is Pillared assembly hall (20 pillars in 4 rows)?
2.x: Pillared assembly hall (20 pillars in 4 rows) – Mohenjodaro

2.s: At which site was the so-called college of priests found?
2.x: College of priests – Mohenjodaro

2.s: How many fire altars were found at Kalibangan?
2.x: Fire altars – Kalibangan (seven), Lothal, Banawali, Rakhigarhi

2.s: What did the Harappan granaries mainly store?
2.x: Granaries stored the farm surplus (cereals probably taken as tax).

2.s: At which site were Cemetery H and Cemetery R-37 found?
2.x: Cemetery H, R-37, coffin burial, wheat and barley in a wooden mortar, dice, unicorn seal – Harappa

2.s: At which Harappan site was a dockyard found?
2.x: Dockyard – Lothal

2.s: At which Harappan site were horse bones found?
2.x: Horse bones – Surkotada

2.s: At which Harappan site was a bronze chariot found?
2.x: Bronze chariot – Daimabad

2.s: At which site were granaries built in two rows of six?
2.x: Great Granary = Mohenjodaro; two rows of six = Harappa.

2.s: What was the shape of the town plan of Dholavira?
2.x: Location – Kachchh (Khadir island), Gujarat; rectangular plan

2.s: Where in Dholavira lay its stadium (about 283 × 47 m)?
2.x: Stadium – About 283 × 47 m, between the citadel and the middle town

2.s: What kind of burial structures were found at Dholavira?
2.x: Burials – Special cemetery structures

2.s: Which gate of Dholavira was the ten-sign signboard found near?
2.x: Signboard – Ten-sign signboard near the North Gate – the largest Harappan signs

2.s: Which was the first Harappan site in India to become a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
2.x: UNESCO 2021 – India's 40th World Heritage Site; the first IVC site in India on the list

3.s: At which site were the Pashupati seal, the Dancing Girl and the Priest-King found?
3.x: Great Granary, Great Bath, Pashupati seal, Dancing Girl, Priest-King – Mohenjodaro

3.s: At which site was a famous stone male torso found?
3.x: Granaries in two rows of six; Cemeteries R-37 and H; red sandstone torso – Harappa

3.s: Where is Bead factory, furnace, lipstick, ink pot; no citadel?
3.x: Bead factory, furnace, lipstick, ink pot; no citadel – Chanhudaro

3.s: At which Harappan site were camel bones found, along with the earliest ploughed field?
3.x: Earliest ploughed field, seven fire altars, camel bones, wooden drain – Kalibangan

3.s: Where is Terracotta (toy) plough, radial streets, barley?
3.x: Terracotta (toy) plough, radial streets, barley – Banawali

3.s: Where is Horse bones (doubtful), pot burials?
3.x: Horse bones (doubtful), pot burials – Surkotada

3.s: Which Harappan city was laid out in three parts, with a stadium and rock-cut stepwells?
3.x: Reservoirs, stadium, 10-sign signboard, three-part town, rock-cut stepwells – Dholavira

3.s: Which bronze animal figures were found at Daimabad along with the chariot?
3.x: Bronze (copper) chariot, bronze buffalo, rhinoceros, elephant – Daimabad

3.s: Where is Rice, bajra, sorghum; Late Harappan?
3.x: Rice, bajra, sorghum; Late Harappan – Rangpur

3.s: Where is Largest site in India; granary; gemstone factory?
3.x: Largest site in India; granary; gemstone factory – Rakhigarhi

3.s: Where is Dog buried with a human; oval pit burials?
3.x: Dog buried with a human; oval pit burials – Ropar

3.s: Where is 125 graves; human burials?
3.x: 125 graves; human burials – Sinauli (Sanauli)

3.s: At which Harappan site was the earliest garlic found?
3.x: Earliest garlic – Balu

3.s: Which Harappan sites are known for shell objects?
3.x: Shell objects – Nageshwar, Balakot

3.s: Where is Lapis lazuli trade outpost; canals?
3.x: Lapis lazuli trade outpost; canals – Shortughai (Afghanistan)

3.s: At which Harappan site was the earliest furnace found?
3.x: Earliest furnace – Kot Bala

3.s: Which Harappan site is known for salt production?
3.x: Salt production – Kerala-no-dhoro

3.s: Which Harappan site has a Gujarati name that also means "Mound of the Dead"?
3.x: Names – Mohenjodaro = "Mound of the Dead" (Sindhi; Lothal means the same in Gujarati); Kalibangan = "black bangles"; Dholavira's local name = Kotada

3.s: At which Harappan site was a ship seal found?
3.x: Seals – Cylindrical seals: Kalibangan and Mohenjodaro; ship seal: Lothal

3.s: When are the horse bones at Surkotada dated to?
3.x: Surkotada horse bones – Dated c. 2100–1700 BCE

3.s: What typical Harappan object with Indus script was found at Ropar?
3.x: Ropar (Sutlej, Punjab) – A typical Harappan steatite seal with Indus script

3.s: When did the earthquake at the end of Kalibangan's early phase occur?
3.x: Earthquake – Earliest Harappan evidence at Kalibangan (end of its early phase, c. 2700 BCE)

3.s: At which site did Wheeler read the skeletons in wells and streets as a "massacre"?
3.x: Skeletons in wells and streets: Mohenjodaro (late level) – Wheeler's "massacre"; now read as multiple burials.

3.s: At which Harappan site was a toy plough found?
3.x: Horse remains = Surkotada; ploughed field = Kalibangan; toy plough = Banawali.

3.s: Which gulf does the port town of Lothal lie near?
3.x: Location – Ahmedabad, Gujarat, on the Bhogava (tributary of the Sabarmati), near the Gulf of Khambhat

3.s: Which site was the port city of the IVC, called 'Mini Harappa'?
3.x: Role – The port city of the IVC; called "Mini Harappa"

3.s: What are the dimensions of the brick-lined tidal dock at Lothal?
3.x: Dock – Dockyard: a brick-lined basin 218 m × 37 m with sluice gates – the world's earliest tidal dock

3.s: In which years did S. R. Rao excavate Lothal?
3.x: Excavation – Discovered 1954, excavated 1955–60 by S.R. Rao

3.s: Which Harappan port town yielded rice husk, a bead-making factory and three double burials?
3.x: Other finds – Rice husk, fire altars, bead-making factory, Persian Gulf (button) seal, ship on a seal, terracotta ship, copper dog, chess-like game set, three double burials, painted jar (cunning fox story), ivory scale

3.s: Which of these, besides Lothal, was a Harappan port?
3.x: Ports – Other ports: Rangpur, Somnath (Prabhas Patan), Balakot, Kuntasi, Khirasara, Sutkagendor

3.s: At which Harappan site in Gujarat is the National Maritime Heritage Complex being built?
3.x: Site – NMHC is being built at Lothal, Gujarat

3.s: Which Union ministry is building the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal?
3.x: Ministry – Ports, Shipping and Waterways

3.s: When did the Union Cabinet approve the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal?
3.x: Approval – Union Cabinet, October 2024

3.s: How complete was Phase 1A of the Lothal maritime heritage complex as of September 2026?
3.x: Progress – As of Sep 2026: Phase 1A about 82% complete; target 31 Oct 2026

3.s: What is Phase 1B of the National Maritime Heritage Complex at Lothal meant to add?
o: Eight galleries and a lighthouse museum
3.x: Phase 1B – To add eight galleries and a lighthouse museum

3.s: In which province of which country does Harappa lie today?
3.x: Harappa – Daya Ram Sahni (1921) – Ravi – Punjab (Pakistan)

3.s: In which district of Sindh does Mohenjodaro lie?
3.x: Mohenjodaro – R.D. Banerji (1922) – Indus – Larkana, Sindh (Pakistan)

3.s: In which province of Pakistan is Chanhudaro?
3.x: Chanhudaro – N.G. Majumdar (1931); Mackay 1935–36 – Indus – Sindh (Pakistan)

3.s: In which district of Gujarat is Lothal?
3.x: Lothal – S.R. Rao (1954–57) – Bhogava – Ahmedabad, Gujarat

3.s: In which district of Rajasthan is Kalibangan?
3.x: Kalibangan – A. Ghosh (1953); B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar (1960–69) – Ghaggar – Hanumangarh, Rajasthan

3.s: Which archaeologist later continued the excavations at Rakhigarhi after Amarendra Nath?
3.x: Rakhigarhi – Amarendra Nath (1997); later Vasant Shinde – Ghaggar–Drishadvati – Hisar, Haryana

3.s: In which river basin does Rakhigarhi lie?
3.x: Rakhigarhi – Amarendra Nath (1997); later Vasant Shinde – Ghaggar–Drishadvati – Hisar, Haryana

3.s: In which district of Gujarat is Surkotada?
3.x: Surkotada – J.P. Joshi (1964) – Kachchh, Gujarat

3.s: Who excavated Rangpur in 1953–54?
3.x: Rangpur – M.S. Vats (1931); S.R. Rao (1953–54) – Sukhbhadar – Gujarat

3.s: In which present-day state is the Harappan site of Rangpur?
3.x: Rangpur – M.S. Vats (1931); S.R. Rao (1953–54) – Sukhbhadar – Gujarat

3.s: Which of these Harappan sites is in Haryana, not in Gujarat?
3.x: Gujarat sites: Surkotada, Lothal, Dholavira; Banawali is in Haryana.

3.s: Who excavated the Harappan port of Lothal?
3.x: S.R. Rao = Lothal; R.S. Bisht = Banawali and Dholavira; J.P. Joshi = Surkotada; A. Ghosh = Kalibangan.

3.s: Which archaeologist excavated both Banawali and Dholavira?
3.x: S.R. Rao = Lothal; R.S. Bisht = Banawali and Dholavira; J.P. Joshi = Surkotada; A. Ghosh = Kalibangan.

3.s: Which site in Kachchh, besides Surkotada, is a Harappan site?
3.x: Surkotada, Desalpur (Kachchh) – Harappan

3.s: Which cultural phases are found at Kot Diji in Sindh?
3.x: Kot Diji, Chanhudaro (Sindh) – Harappan (Kot Diji also pre-Harappan)

3.s: What does the Mauryan-era copper plate from Sohgaura deal with?
3.x: Sohgaura (Gorakhpur, UP, on the Rapti) – Not Harappan – a Mauryan-era copper plate on famine granaries

3.s: Which of these is NOT a Harappan site?
3.x: Pataliputra – Not Harappan

3.s: How many mounds does Rakhigarhi have, according to Vasant Shinde?
3.x: Rakhigarhi (Hisar, Haryana) – The largest Harappan site (about 350–550 ha; 11 mounds per Shinde)

3.s: Which Harappan site is regarded as the oldest?
3.x: Bhirrana – The oldest site

3.s: Which was the first Harappan site excavated after Independence?
3.x: First after Independence – Ropar

3.s: What is the UNESCO status of Rakhigarhi?
3.x: Rakhigarhi – Tentative List

3.s: Which Harappan site gave ancient DNA lacking the "Steppe Pastoralist" gene, challenging the Aryan-invasion view?
3.x: Rakhigarhi DNA: the ~4,600-year-old female skeleton lacked the "Steppe Pastoralist" gene → read as indigenous ancestry, challenging the Aryan-invasion view.

3.s: How many skeletons has the Mound 7 cemetery at Rakhigarhi yielded?
3.x: Mound 7 cemetery: 56 skeletons; the dig of 23 Jun 2026 found five complete skeletons (aged 30–40) and three fragmentary burials.

4.s: Which was the first metal used by man, with which the chalcolithic cultures began?
4.x: Copper – The first metal used by man; the chalcolithic cultures began with it

4.s: Which of these metals did the Harappans use?
4.x: Harappan metals – Copper, bronze, gold, silver, lead

4.s: Which famous Harappan bronze figure was made by the lost-wax process?
4.x: Alloy – Bronze = copper + tin; tools, weapons and the Dancing Girl (lost-wax casting)

4.s: Which kind of metal object far outnumbers the others among Harappan finds?
4.x: Copper and bronze – Pure copper objects far outnumber bronze ones

4.s: Which metal did the Harappans pioneer in India, importing it from Afghanistan?
4.x: Silver – Harappans pioneered silver use; silver imported (Afghanistan)

4.s: From which mines in Rajasthan did the Harappans get copper?
4.x: Copper – Khetri mines (Rajasthan); also Oman (Magan)

4.s: Where did the Harappans get their tin from?
4.x: Tin – Afghanistan, Iran

4.s: Where in India did the Harappans get their gold from?
4.x: Gold – Karnataka (Kolar), Afghanistan

4.s: From which region of Afghanistan did the Harappans get lapis lazuli?
4.x: Lapis lazuli – Badakhshan via Shortughai (Afghanistan)

4.s: Where did the Harappans get their carnelian from?
4.x: Carnelian – Bharuch / Saurashtra (Gujarat)

4.s: Where did the Harappans get their steatite from?
4.x: Steatite – South Rajasthan, north Gujarat

4.s: Which hills in Sindh supplied the chert for mass-produced Harappan blades?
4.x: Chert, limestone (blades) – Sukkur and Rohri hills (Sindh) – mass-produced blades for Sindh

4.s: Which cereal was the main crop of the first farmers of the subcontinent?
4.x: First farmers' crops – Mainly barley, also wheat; sheep, goats, cattle

4.s: When was barley, the first cereal used by man, first used?
4.x: First cereal used by man – Barley (c. 8000 BC)

4.s: Which early farming village of Baluchistan is dated c. 5000–4000 BC?
4.x: Early Baluchistan farming villages – Kili Gul Muhammad (c. 5000–4000 BC), Damb Sadaat, Anjira, Rana Ghundai

4.s: Which site in Sant Kabir Nagar (UP) has the oldest paddy and, per the latest research, the first agriculture?
4.x: First agriculture per the latest research; oldest paddy – Lahuradeva (Sant Kabir Nagar, UP)

4.s: Which site in the Belan valley was once thought to have the oldest paddy?
4.x: Once thought the oldest paddy – Koldihwa (Belan valley, UP)

4.s: At which Neolithic site were cattle pens found along with rice?
4.x: Rice and cattle pens – Mahagara

4.s: Which site on the Kali river, excavated by R. C. Gaur in 1962, gave the earliest iron in India?
4.x: Earliest iron in India – Atranjikhera (Kali river); excavated by R.C. Gaur (1962)

4.s: Which site (7th-3rd millennium BCE) is the Neolithic root of the Harappan civilisation?
4.x: Mehrgarh (7th–3rd millennium BCE) is the Neolithic root of the Harappan civilisation; similar villages at Mundigak (Afghanistan).

4.s: What was the main occupation of the Harappans, whose surplus fed the cities?
4.x: Main occupation = agriculture; the surplus stored in granaries fed the cities.

4.s: At which sites were the largest finds of wheat made?
4.x: Wheat (largest finds) – Harappa; Mehrgarh

4.s: At which sites was the earliest rice husk in South Asia found?
4.x: Rice husk (earliest in South Asia) – Lothal, Rangpur

4.s: At which Harappan sites were millets and rice the staple?
4.x: Millets and rice as staple – Rangpur, Surkotada

4.s: At which site was a woven cotton piece, evidence of Harappan cotton, found?
4.x: Cotton – Mohenjodaro (woven cotton piece); Mehrgarh

4.s: At which Harappan site was evidence of indigo found?
4.x: Indigo – Rojdi

4.s: Which group lists other crops grown by the Harappans?
o: Peas, lentil, chickpea, sesame and mustard
4.x: Other crops – Peas, lentil, chickpea, sesame, mustard, dates, melon, grapes, henna

4.s: What did the Greeks call cotton, after Sindh?
4.x: Cotton: the Harappans were the first to grow cotton and make cotton cloth; the Greeks called it Sindon (from Sindh). The IVC had no coins.

4.s: Who brought maize to India?
4.x: Maize came with the Portuguese. The Rig Vedic economy was pastoral.

4.s: What was the basic nature of the Rig Vedic economy?
4.x: Maize came with the Portuguese. The Rig Vedic economy was pastoral.

4.s: Where is Earliest ploughed field (cross furrows, two crops together)?
4.x: Earliest ploughed field (cross furrows, two crops together) – Kalibangan (Early Harappan level)

4.s: At which Harappan site was a clay plough found?
4.x: Clay plough – Rakhigarhi

4.s: At which Harappan site have traces of canals been found?
4.x: Traces of canals – Shortughai (Afghanistan)

4.s: What kind of ploughs did the Harappans use?
4.x: Wooden ploughs; flood irrigation; canal irrigation inconclusive in Punjab and Sindh; double cropping.

4.s: Which humped breed of cattle was the favoured domesticated animal of the Harappans?
4.x: Domesticated – Humped bull (zebu, favoured), oxen, buffalo, sheep, goat, pig, dog, cat, ass, camel, elephant

4.s: Which group of wild animals was known to the Harappans?
4.x: Wild but known – Elephant, tiger, rhinoceros, deer, gharial

4.s: Which animal is not established in the Harappan culture, with no bones or images in its early and mature levels?
4.x: Not established – Horse – no bones or images in the early and mature levels; only doubtful finds (superficial level at Mohenjodaro, Lothal terracotta, Surkotada bones)

4.s: Which animal has never been found at Harappan sites, neither as remains nor on seals?
4.x: Never found – Lion – no remains and not on seals

4.s: At which Harappan site was a dog found buried with a human?

15.s: Which Later Vedic site in Meerut district lies about 100 km north-east of Delhi?
15.x: Hastinapura (Meerut district, UP) lies about 100 km north-east of Delhi, its nearest modern city.

15.s: Which king of Videha followed Agni Vaishvanara as it burnt the forests eastward?
15.x: Videgha Madhava (Mathava), king of Videha, lived on the Sarasvati; with his priest Gautama Rahugana he followed Agni Vaishvanara (the sacrificial fire) as it burnt the forests eastward.

15.s: Which river did Videgha Madhava cross before settling Videha?
15.x: They crossed the Sadanira (Gandak); the land beyond was settled as Videha – read as eastward movement and agricultural colonisation by burning and clearing forests (fire and iron axes).

15.s: Which sage is said to have Aryanised South India by crossing the Vindhyas?
15.x: Agastya = the sage said to have Aryanised South India (he crossed the Vindhyas).

15.s: Who was the priest of Videgha Madhava on his eastward march?
15.x: Axis of Aryan culture = Kuru-Panchala; Videgha Madhava's priest = Gautama Rahugana; river crossed = Sadanira (Gandak).

15.s: When is Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) dated?
15.x: Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) – 2000–1500 BCE – Chalcolithic

15.s: To which cultural phase does Ochre Coloured Pottery belong?
15.x: Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) – 2000–1500 BCE – Chalcolithic

15.s: When is Black and Red Ware (BRW) dated in the north?
15.x: Black and Red Ware (BRW) – 1450–1200 BCE – Chalcolithic; also Later Vedic; Megalithic south

15.s: With which southern culture is Black and Red Ware also associated?
15.x: Black and Red Ware (BRW) – 1450–1200 BCE – Chalcolithic; also Later Vedic; Megalithic south

15.s: When is Painted Grey Ware (PGW) dated?
15.x: Painted Grey Ware (PGW) – 1200–500 BCE – Early Iron Age / Later Vedic

15.s: With which age is Painted Grey Ware associated?
15.x: Painted Grey Ware (PGW) – 1200–500 BCE – Early Iron Age / Later Vedic

15.s: When is Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) dated?
15.x: Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) – 700–100 BCE (from c. 600 BCE in the Ganga valley) – Mahajanapadas, second urbanisation

15.s: With which phase is Northern Black Polished Ware associated?
15.x: Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) – 700–100 BCE (from c. 600 BCE in the Ganga valley) – Mahajanapadas, second urbanisation

15.s: Which ill-fired red pottery leaves an ochre colour on the fingers?
15.x: OCP is an ill-fired red ware that leaves an ochre colour on the fingers; it was christened (named) at Hastinapur by B.B. Lal (1950–52).

15.s: Which of these is NOT a Later Vedic ware?
15.x: Four wares known to the Later Vedic people: Red Ware (most popular), Black-slipped Ware, Black-and-Red Ware, Painted Grey Ware (most distinctive). NBPW is not a Later Vedic ware (post-Vedic, shiny black).

15.s: Which vessel forms are most common in Painted Grey Ware?
15.x: Ware – Grey pottery with black linear / geometric painted designs; mainly bowls and dishes; deluxe tableware of the upper strata; not polished black

15.s: Which pottery marks the Gangetic plain in 1000–600 BC?
15.x: Period – Pottery of 1000–600 BC in the Gangetic plain = PGW

15.s: How many Painted Grey Ware sites are known, roughly?
15.x: Spread – About 700 sites, mainly in the upper Ganga basin and the Indo-Gangetic divide (Punjab, Haryana, western UP) – not the lower Indus basin

15.s: At which site was Painted Grey Ware first found (1940–44)?
15.x: Discovery – First found at Ahichchhatra (excavations 1940–44); the Hastinapur excavation (1950–52, B.B. Lal) established it as a culture

15.s: From which Rajasthan mines did the copper of the PGW people possibly come?
15.x: Finds – Iron weapons, copper objects (copper possibly from Khetri, Rajasthan), glass, bone, semi-precious beads (trade, barter; no coins)

15.s: In which district is Hastinapur, the Kuru capital and PGW site?
15.x: Hastinapur – Meerut, western UP (Kuru capital)

15.s: In which district of western UP is the PGW site Atranjikhera?
15.x: Atranjikhera – Etah, western UP (Doab)

15.s: In which district of UP is the PGW site Ahichchhatra?
15.x: Ahichchhatra – Bareilly, UP

15.s: Where is Bhagwanpura?
o: Haryana – 13-roomed mud house; pre-iron PGW with Late Harappan pottery
15.x: Bhagwanpura – Haryana – 13-roomed mud house; pre-iron PGW with Late Harappan pottery

15.s: In which state is Noh, with its OCP–BRW–PGW sequence?
15.x: Noh – Rajasthan (OCP–BRW–PGW sequence)

15.s: What did the early PGW of the Ghaggar-Hakra and Bhagwanpura lack?
15.x: Early PGW (Ghaggar-Hakra, Bhagwanpura) has no iron; the later Doab PGW is iron-using.

15.s: Which metal is 'krishna ayas' (black metal) of Later Vedic texts?
15.x: Krishna ayas / Shyama ayas ("black metal") – Iron (Later Vedic texts; first in the Yajurveda)

15.s: Which metal is 'lohita ayas' in Vedic texts?
15.x: Lohita ayas – Copper

15.s: Which metal is 'hiranya' in Vedic texts?
15.x: Hiranya – Gold

15.s: What did 'nishka' become later, after being a gold ornament?
15.x: Nishka – Gold ornament; later a unit of value

15.s: When, approximately, is iron technology in North India dated?
15.x: Date – Iron technology about 1000–800 BCE; common at most PGW sites of the Doab

15.s: When did iron arrowheads and spearheads become common in western UP?
15.x: Weapons – Iron arrowheads and spearheads common in western UP from about 800 BCE

15.s: What cleared the Gangetic forests in the Later Vedic period?
15.x: Forest clearance – Iron axes and fire cleared the Gangetic forests; iron reached Kosala and Videha by the end of the period

15.s: Which classic northern site has the earliest iron, as excavated by R.C. Gaur?
15.x: Earliest iron among the classic northern sites – Atranjikhera (Etah, UP; excavated by R.C. Gaur)

15.s: Which Gandhara site is among the early iron sites of c. 1000 BC?
15.x: Other early sites – Hastinapur, Kaushambi, Taxila (Gandhara, c. 1000 BC)

15.s: At which UP site was iron found in the Black and Red Ware phase, before 1200 BCE?
15.x: Jakhera (UP) – Iron in the Black and Red Ware phase, before 1200 BCE

15.s: When, approximately, is iron at Dharwar (Karnataka) dated?
15.x: Dharwar (Karnataka) – Iron c. 1000 BCE

15.s: In which Tamil Nadu district is Sivagalai, with the oldest iron dates?
15.x: Sivagalai – Thoothukudi – Iron dated to about 2953 BCE (to 3345 BCE) – now the oldest (Tamil Nadu report, Jan 2025)

15.s: When, per the Tamil Nadu report of Jan 2025, is the iron of Sivagalai dated?
15.x: Sivagalai – Thoothukudi – Iron dated to about 2953 BCE (to 3345 BCE) – now the oldest (Tamil Nadu report, Jan 2025)

15.s: In which Tamil Nadu district is Mayiladumparai?
15.x: Mayiladumparai – Krishnagiri – Iron AMS-dated to 2172 BCE; the earliest claim before Sivagalai

15.s: To which year is the iron of Mayiladumparai AMS-dated?
15.x: Mayiladumparai – Krishnagiri – Iron AMS-dated to 2172 BCE; the earliest claim before Sivagalai

15.s: In which Tamil Nadu district is Thirumalapuram, with an Iron Age urn chamber?
15.x: Thirumalapuram – Tenkasi – Iron Age urn chamber

15.s: In which Tamil Nadu district is Adichanallur?
15.x: Adichanallur – Thoothukudi – Urn burials; not a PGW or northern iron site

15.s: What kind of site is Adichanallur in Tamil Nadu?
15.x: Adichanallur – Thoothukudi – Urn burials; not a PGW or northern iron site

15.s: What do the early Tamil Nadu iron dates tell us about where PGW began?
o: That it began in Tamil Nadu
15.x: These dates push iron use far earlier than the Gangetic 1000 BCE; they say nothing about where PGW began.

15.s: From which language do the roots of the word 'Chalcolithic' (copper-stone) come?
15.x: First metal used in India = copper (Chalcolithic = the "copper-stone" age, Greek *khalkos* + *lithos*); iron came later.

15.s: How many oxen, at most, drew Later Vedic ploughs?
15.x: Agriculture became the main livelihood; the wooden ploughshare was common; ploughs were drawn by 6, 8, 12 and even 24 oxen.

15.s: At which sites have rice remains of the 8th c. BCE been found?
15.x: Rice – Vrihi (ritual use; rice remains of the 8th c. BCE at Hastinapur, Atranjikhera)

15.s: In which phase did true towns such as Shravasti and Kausambi arise in the Ganga valley?
15.x: Settlements: mainly villages of mud-brick and wattle-and-daub houses; burnt bricks not common; Hastinapur and Kaushambi only proto-urban; true towns came in the NBPW phase (second urbanisation: Shravasti, Kausambi, Hastinapur).

15.s: What were the merchant groups of the Later Vedic period called?
15.x: Crafts: carpentry (chariots), leather, pottery, weaving (by women), copper, bronze and iron smiths; Shresthins = merchant groups; units of value nishka, satamana, krishnala; barter still the main mode.

15.s: Which culture represents the Iron Age in Andhra?
15.x: Andhra: the Iron Age in Andhra = the Megalithic culture with BRW (Brahmagiri, Nagarjunakonda, Gudivada, Jonnawada); H.D. Sankalia: rice was first harvested in AP in the Iron Age (Megalithic) era.

15.s: When, per pre-NBPW pottery from Rajghat, did Varanasi's urban origins begin?
15.x: Sep 2026: BHU opened 22 sealed boxes of 10,000+ Rajghat (Varanasi) artefacts; pre-NBPW pottery dates Varanasi's urban origins to about 800 BCE.

15.s: Which god, the creator, became supreme in the Later Vedic period?
15.x: Prajapati – Creator; became supreme

15.s: Which god, minor in the Rig Veda, rose as the preserver in Later Vedic times?
15.x: Vishnu – Rose as the preserver (minor in the Rigveda)

15.s: Which Later Vedic god of animals later merged with Shiva?
15.x: Rudra – God of animals; later merged with Shiva

15.s: Which Later Vedic cattle god became the god of the Shudras?
15.x: Pushan – Cattle god; god of the Shudras

15.s: Which gods lost importance in the Later Vedic period?
15.x: Indra, Agni, Varuna – Lost importance

15.s: What grew in the Later Vedic period while prayers declined, raising the priests' power?
15.x: Prayers declined and elaborate sacrifices grew, raising the priests' power; Upanishadic thinkers criticised ritualism.

15.s: Which Vedic priest recited the Rigveda at the sacrifice?
15.x: Hotri – Recited the Rigveda

15.s: Which Vedic priest, of the Yajurveda, did the manual work of the sacrifice?
15.x: Adhvaryu – Yajurveda; did the practical, manual work of the sacrifice

15.s: Which Vedic priest chanted the Samaveda?
15.x: Udgatri – Chanted the Samaveda

15.s: Which Vedic priest, of the Atharvaveda, supervised the sacrifice?
15.x: Brahman – Atharvaveda; supervised

16.s: Which Later Vedic kingdom held the Delhi–Meerut region with Hastinapur and Kurukshetra?
16.x: Kuru – Delhi–Meerut / upper Doab; Hastinapur, Kurukshetra

16.s: Where is Panchala?
16.x: Panchala – Middle Doab–Rohilkhand; Ahichchhatra

16.s: In which region was the Later Vedic kingdom of Kosala?
16.x: Kosala – Eastern UP

16.s: In which region did the Later Vedic kingdom of Kashi lie?
16.x: Kashi – Varanasi region

16.s: Where is Videha?
o: Mewar – Sitaram Das, then Vijay Singh Pathik
Maharashtra – the southernmost Late Harappan site
North Bihar, beyond the Sadanira (Gandak); King Janaka
16.x: Videha – North Bihar, beyond the Sadanira (Gandak); King Janaka

16.s: Which kingdoms rose in the east after Kuru-Panchala, leading to the Mahajanapadas?
16.x: Kuru-Panchala dominated the upper Ganga valley; Kosala, Kashi and Videha then rose in the east → the Mahajanapadas.

16.s: Of which kingdom was the Upanishadic king Janaka the ruler?
16.x: Janaka – Videha

16.s: Of which kingdom was the Upanishadic king Ashvapati the ruler?
16.x: Ashvapati – Kekaya

16.s: Of which kingdom was the Upanishadic king Ajatashatru (not Magadha's) the ruler?
16.x: Ajatashatru – Kashi (a different king from Magadha's Ajatashatru)

16.s: Of which kingdom was the Upanishadic king Pravahana Jaivali the ruler?
16.x: Pravahana Jaivali – Panchala

16.s: Which royal sacrifice was the king's consecration and included the Ratnahavimshi?
16.x: Rajasuya – Royal consecration; conferred supreme power; includes the Ratnahavimshi (offerings at the Ratnins' houses)

16.s: What did the Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice) assert?
16.x: Ashvamedha – Horse sacrifice; supremacy over other kings and control of the area the horse roamed

16.s: Which royal sacrifice, the 'drink of strength', had a chariot race won by the king?
16.x: Vajapeya – "Drink of strength"; a chariot race won by the king over his kinsmen

16.s: What was the Punarabhisheka at the end of the Rajasuya?
16.x: Punarabhisheka – Second anointing at the end of the Rajasuya

16.s: Which of these is a Chola-period title, NOT a Vedic royal sacrifice?
16.x: Muvendavelan is a title (a Chola-period chief), not a royal sacrifice.

16.s: How many cows could be given as dakshina in a Rajasuya?
16.x: Large Shrauta sacrifices needed many priests and heavy dakshina (up to 2,40,000 cows in a Rajasuya) → they strengthened the Brahmanas.

16.s: At which Andhra site has an Ashvamedha altar been found?
16.x: In Andhra: the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Vishnukundins performed these rites; Ikshvaku titles: Vajapeya = Samrat / Virat; Ashvamedha = Swarat; an Ashvamedha altar at Nagarjunakonda.

16.s: Which Ikshvaku title went with the Vajapeya sacrifice?
16.x: In Andhra: the Satavahanas, Ikshvakus and Vishnukundins performed these rites; Ikshvaku titles: Vajapeya = Samrat / Virat; Ashvamedha = Swarat; an Ashvamedha altar at Nagarjunakonda.

16.s: Who did the Vajapeya sacrifice assert the king's superiority over?
16.x: Ashvamedha = over other kings; Vajapeya = over kinsmen; Rajasuya = consecration.

16.s: Which Vedic assembly disappeared in the Later Vedic period?
16.x: The Vidatha disappeared; the Sabha and Samiti continued but declined, dominated by chiefs, nobles and Brahmanas; women no longer sat in the Sabha; village assemblies tried local cases.

16.s: What did bali become in the Later Vedic period?
16.x: Bali – Tribute: voluntary in the Rigveda, now regular and compulsory – the king's tax on the people

16.s: What usual share of the produce was the Later Vedic 'bhaga' taken by the king?
16.x: Bhaga – The king's share of the produce (one-sixth; texts give 1/6 to 1/2)

16.s: What was 'shulka' in the Later Vedic period?
16.x: Shulka – Customs / tolls

16.s: Which varna were the main tribute-payers of the Later Vedic period?
16.x: The Vaishyas were the main (only) tribute-payers; the Bhagadugha collected and the Sangrahitri managed the revenue.

16.s: What did 'varman' mean in Vedic usage?
16.x: Varman = armour and Vidatha = assembly – neither is a tax.

16.s: In which texts does the word 'rashtra' first appear?
16.x: Jana (tribe) → janapada / rashtra (territory); the word rashtra first appears in the Later Vedic texts; tribal chiefdom → hereditary territorial monarchy, which prepared the way for the Mahajanapadas (6th century BCE).

16.s: How did Later Vedic kingship usually pass?
o: By hereditary succession to the eldest son
16.x: Kingship was hereditary, usually to the eldest son (primogeniture); men became rajas by performing big sacrifices; traces of election survived. Kingship was not traced to election by village assemblies.

16.s: Which Later Vedic title meant the sole or paramount ruler?
16.x: Ekarat (Atharvaveda, Aitareya Brahmana) = the sole / paramount ruler.

16.s: Which ruler's title was used in the east in Later Vedic times?
16.x: East – Samrat

16.s: Which ruler's title was used in the south in Later Vedic times?
16.x: South – Bhoja

16.s: Which ruler's title was used in the west in Later Vedic times?
16.x: West – Svarat

16.s: Which ruler's title was used in the north in Later Vedic times?
16.x: North – Virat

16.s: Which of these is NOT a state form listed in the Aitareya Brahmana?
16.x: State forms in the Aitareya Brahmana: Rajya, Bhojya, Swarajya, Vairajya, Samrajya; Ganatantra is not one of them.

16.s: Which text has the earliest account of the gods choosing a king to lead them against the Asuras?
16.x: Aitareya Brahmana – Earliest account: the gods, losing to the Asuras, chose a king to lead them; king = protector of Brahmins

16.s: Which Brahmana puts forward the theory of the divine origin of kingship?
16.x: Taittiriya Brahmana – Theory of the divine origin of kingship

16.s: With which god does the Shatapatha Brahmana link the king?
16.x: Shatapatha Brahmana – Linked the king with Prajapati; the Rajasuya and Vajapeya gave him divine qualities

16.s: What was the Later Vedic king, in contrast to the Rigvedic elective chief?
16.x: Tribe; cattle; elective chief – Territory; agriculture; hereditary king

16.s: Which council of royal functionaries appeared with the Later Vedic decline of the assemblies?
16.x: Voluntary bali; strong assemblies – Compulsory taxes (bali, bhaga, shulka); assemblies decline; Ratnins

16.s: What was the king of the east called in the Later Vedic age?
16.x: East = Samrat, North = Virat; the word rashtra first appears now.

16.s: In which period does the word 'rashtra' first appear?
16.x: East = Samrat, North = Virat; the word rashtra first appears now.

16.s: What were the Later Vedic king's 12 royal functionaries, honoured in the Rajasuya, called?
16.x: Ratnins ("jewels") = the king's council of 12 royal functionaries: purohita, rajan, mahishi, senani, bhagadugha, sangrahitri, suta, kshata, govikartana, gramani, parivakti, akshavapa (some add palagala); honoured in the Ratnahavimshi rite of the Rajasuya.

16.s: What was the function of the Purohita among the Ratnins?
16.x: Purohita – Chief priest

16.s: What was the function of the Senani among the Ratnins?
16.x: Senani – Army chief

16.s: What was the function of the Suta among the Ratnins?
16.x: Suta – Charioteer and herald

16.s: Which Ratnin collected the king's share of revenue?
16.x: Bhagadugha – Revenue collector (king's share)

16.s: What was the function of the Sangrahitri among the Ratnins?
16.x: Sangrahitri – Treasurer

16.s: Which Ratnin was the accountant and superintendent of dice?
16.x: Akshavapa – Accountant; superintendent of dice

16.s: What was the function of the Palagala among the Ratnins?
16.x: Palagala – Messenger

16.s: Which of these did the Later Vedic king still lack?
16.x: More officers, but no regular bureaucracy and no standing army.

16.s: Which Later Vedic ratnin collected the taxes?
16.x: Bhagadugha collects; Sangrahitri stores.

16.s: Which Later Vedic ratnin stored the revenue as treasurer?
16.x: Bhagadugha collects; Sangrahitri stores.

17.s: What did varna come to rest on in the Later Vedic period?
17.x: Society was stratified in the order Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra = the Varna system (varna came to rest on birth; the spread of jatis is post-Vedic).

17.s: Which Later Vedic varna were the priests and teachers, the most powerful group?
17.x: Brahmana – Priests, teachers; most powerful

17.s: What was the role of the Kshatriyas (Rajanya) in Later Vedic society?
17.x: Kshatriya (Rajanya) – Rulers, warriors

17.s: Which Later Vedic varna were the only tribute-payers?
17.x: Vaishya – Farmers, herders, traders, artisans; the only tribute-payers

17.s: Which Later Vedic varna was denied upanayana, Vedic study and the Sabha?
17.x: Shudra – Service; no upanayana, no Vedas, no Sabha

17.s: Where is the first statement of the four varnas found?
17.x: First statement of the four varnas – Purusha Sukta, Rigveda 10th Mandala

17.s: Who were the Dvija (twice-born) of Later Vedic society?
17.x: Dvija (twice-born) – The upper three varnas, entitled to upanayana

17.s: Which Brahmana calls the Shudra 'servant of another', who could be expelled or beaten at will?
17.x: Aitareya Brahmana – Shudra = "servant of another", who could be expelled or beaten at will

17.s: Which groups stood outside the Later Vedic varna order?
17.x: Outside the varna order – Vratyas, Nishadas

17.s: What is the combined scheme of the four social orders and four life stages called?
17.x: Varna + ashrama – Varnashrama Dharma

17.s: Which Upanishad names the Chandala as a person of despised birth?
17.x: The Chhandogya Upanishad names the Chandala as a person of despised birth – an early sign only; untouchability was absent in the Rigvedic age.

17.s: In which phase did untouchability take a clear, formal shape?
17.x: Untouchability took clear, formal shape in the Dharmashastra phase (early Christian era), not in the Rigvedic or Later Vedic phase.

17.s: Who was the Sarthavaha in ancient Indian trade?
17.x: Sarthavaha (caravan leader, head of a trade guild / Srenipramukh) = a Vaishya; guild rules = Samay, Srenidharma; Vaishya guilds (gana) were headed by a Shreshthin.

17.s: Which text has the first reference to money-lending?
17.x: The first reference to money-lending is in the Shatapatha Brahmana; usurer = kusidin.

17.s: What was the duty of a person in the Brahmacharya ashrama?
17.x: Brahmacharya – Student; Vedic study

17.s: Which ashrama required the daily Pancha Mahayajnas?
17.x: Grihastha – Householder; daily Pancha Mahayajnas

17.s: Which ashrama meant gradual withdrawal to the forest?
17.x: Vanaprastha – Gradual withdrawal (forest)

17.s: Which ashrama, meaning complete renunciation, was added last?
17.x: Sannyasa – Complete renunciation; added last

17.s: When did the custom of the four ashramas emerge?
17.x: The four ashramas are a custom that emerged in the post-Vedic (Later Vedic) period; the varnas go back to the Rigveda's Purusha Sukta, and Indra, Surya, Rudra and the Maruts are Rigvedic gods.

17.s: Which Upanishad first mentions all four ashramas?
17.x: Only the first three were established in Later Vedic times: the first three appear in the Chhandogya Upanishad; all four first in the Jabala Upanishad.

17.s: Which Upanishad first mentions the first three ashramas?
17.x: Only the first three were established in Later Vedic times: the first three appear in the Chhandogya Upanishad; all four first in the Jabala Upanishad.

17.s: To what is the Brahma yajna of the Pancha Mahayajnas devoted?
17.x: Brahma – Vedic study

17.s: To whom is the Deva yajna of the Pancha Mahayajnas offered?
17.x: Deva – Gods

17.s: To whom is the Pitri yajna of the Pancha Mahayajnas offered?
17.x: Pitri – Ancestors

17.s: To whom is the Bhuta yajna of the Pancha Mahayajnas offered?
17.x: Bhuta – Living beings

17.s: What does the Nri (Atithi) yajna of the Pancha Mahayajnas consist of?
17.x: Nri / Atithi – Hospitality to guests

17.s: Which Purushartha was added later to the trivarga under Upanishadic ideas?
17.x: Purusharthas: Dharma (duty), Artha (wealth), Kama (desire) = the trivarga; Moksha (liberation) was added later under Upanishadic ideas.

17.s: What does the word 'gotra' literally mean?
17.x: Gotra literally = cow-pen (the word first occurs in the Rigveda, meaning a cow shelter); as a clan descended from a common male ancestor it was established in Later Vedic (post-Vedic) times; the Atharvaveda mentions gotra in the lineage sense.

17.s: Which rule forbids marriage within the same gotra?
17.x: Gotra exogamy: no marriage within the same gotra (with caste endogamy and sapinda rules).

17.s: What does the kinship term 'Kula' mean?
17.x: Kula – Family

17.s: What does the kinship term 'Vamsha' mean?
17.x: Vamsha – Lineage

17.s: What does 'Gotra' mean as a kinship term in Later Vedic times?
17.x: Gotra – Clan

17.s: What does 'Kosa' mean?
17.x: Kosa – Treasury (not a kinship term)

17.s: Who wrote 'Kinship Organization in India' (1953), describing four kinship zones?
17.x: Irawati Karve: *Kinship Organization in India* (1953) – four kinship zones.

17.s: How many samskaras (shodasha) are traditionally counted?
17.x: Samskaras = 16 (shodasha): 3 before birth (Garbhadhana, Pumsavana, Simantonnayana), Jatakarma, Chudakarma (tonsure, 3rd year) … Upanayana, Vivaha, Antyeshti.

17.s: In which year of a boy's life was the upanayana usually performed?
17.x: Upanayana = the sacred-thread initiation into Vedic study for the upper three varnas, in the boy's 8th year; fully described in the Shatapatha Brahmana; Shudras and women excluded.

17.s: In which metre was the upanayana mantra given to a Brahmana boy?
17.x: Brahmana – Gayatri

17.s: In which metre was the upanayana mantra given to a Kshatriya boy?
17.x: Kshatriya – Trishtubh

17.s: In which metre was the upanayana mantra given to a Vaishya boy?
17.x: Vaishya – Jagati

17.s: What happened to the status of women in the Later Vedic period?

18.s: Who narrated the Mahabharata to Janamejaya?

272.s: Which Paramara ruler was called Navasahasanka?
272.x: Rulers – Siyaka II, Munja, Sindhuraja (Navasahasanka), Bhoja (c. 1010–1055); last Mahalakadeva (killed 1305 by Alauddin's forces)

272.s: Who wrote the Navasahasanka Charita on the Paramaras?
272.x: Sources – Navasahasanka Charita of Padmagupta (on the Paramaras – Sindhuraja), Prabandha Chintamani of Merutunga, Udaipur Prashasti (genealogy, praises Bhoja), Harsola plates

272.s: Which work: Architecture, town planning and mechanical devices / artificial scientific equipment (yantras)?
272.x: Samarangana Sutradhara – Architecture, town planning and mechanical devices / artificial scientific equipment (yantras)

272.s: What is the subject of Bhoja's Saraswati-Kanthabharana?
272.x: Saraswati-Kanthabharana – Poetics and grammar

272.s: Which work of Bhoja is a commentary on the Yoga-sutra?
272.x: Rajamartanda (Bhojavritti), Yuktikalpataru, Rajamriganka, Champu-Ramayana, Sringara Prakasa – Yoga-sutra commentary, polity, astronomy, poetry

272.s: Which goddess's temple is the Bhojshala at Dhar?
272.x: Bhojshala, Dhar – Centre of Sanskrit learning; temple of Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi); Muslims call it Kamal Maula Mosque

272.s: Which court declared the Bhojshala at Dhar a Hindu temple in May 2026?
272.x: Bhojshala in the news – ASI survey ordered 2024 (under a 2003 ASI arrangement both communities worshipped on separate days); May 2026 – Madhya Pradesh High Court declared it a Hindu temple on ASI findings

272.s: To which god is the unfinished Bhojpur (Bhojeshwar) temple dedicated?
272.x: Bhojpur (Bhojeshwar) temple – Unfinished Shiva temple, Raisen district, beside Bhoja's man-made lake (Bhojtal)

272.s: Which Paramara king built the Tribhuvan Narayan temple at Chittor?
272.x: Tribhuvan Narayan temple, Chittor (now Samiddheshwar) – Built by Paramara Raja Bhoja; restored by Rana Mokal

272.s: Who built the Vijaya Stambha at Chittor?
272.x: Vijaya Stambha, Chittor – Built by Rana Kumbha for his victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa (1440–48)

272.s: Who composed the Kirti-Stambha Prashasti with his father Atri?
272.x: Kirti-Stambha Prashasti – Composed by Atri and his son Mahesh (Atri Kavi); work overseen by architect Jaita

272.s: Which Tirthankara is the Jain Kirti Stambha at Chittor dedicated to?
272.x: Jain Kirti Stambha, Chittor – Merchant Jijaji (Jeeja), 12th c.; dedicated to Adinath

272.s: Who built the Kumbhalgarh fort?
272.x: Kumbhalgarh fort – Rana Kumbha

272.s: Which work on music was written by Rana Kumbha?
272.x: Kumbha on music – Sangeet Raj, Sangeet Mimansa, Rasik Priya (Gita Govinda commentary) – the Rajput ruler who wrote on music

272.s: Which of these was a court scholar of Rana Kumbha?
272.x: Kumbha's court scholars – Muni Sundar Suri, Natha, Tilla Bhatt, Mandan, Kanha Vyas (Muni Jin Vijay was a 20th-century scholar)

272.s: Against whom did Rani Padmini perform jauhar at Chittor?
272.x: Rani Padmini's jauhar at Chittor – Against Alauddin Khalji

272.s: In which language is the Prithviraj Raso written?
272.x: Prithviraj Raso (Braj epic) – Chand Bardai, court poet of Prithviraj – Prithviraj Chauhan; only a 12th-c. nucleus, present text 16th–17th c.

272.s: Who wrote Prithviraja Vijaya?
272.x: Prithviraja Vijaya – Jayanaka (Kashmiri poet) – Prithviraj

272.s: Who wrote Alha Khand?
272.x: Alha Khand – Jagnik – Chandela Paramardi (Parmardidev)

272.s: Who wrote the Alha Khand on the Chandela Paramardi's court?
272.x: Alha Khand – Jagnik – Chandela Paramardi (Parmardidev)

272.s: Who wrote Bisaldeva Raso?
272.x: Bisaldeva Raso – Narapati Nalha – Vigraharaja IV

272.s: Which Chauhan king is the subject of the Bisaldeva Raso?
272.x: Bisaldeva Raso – Narapati Nalha – Vigraharaja IV

272.s: Who wrote Khuman Raso?
272.x: Khuman Raso – Dalpati Vijay – Mewar

272.s: Which kingdom is the subject of Dalpati Vijay's Khuman Raso?
272.x: Khuman Raso – Dalpati Vijay – Mewar

272.s: Who wrote Shatrusal Raso?
272.x: Shatrusal Raso – Dungar Singh

272.s: Who wrote Lalita Vigraharaja (play)?
272.x: Lalita Vigraharaja (play) – Somadeva – Vigraharaja IV

272.s: Who wrote Harakeli Nataka?
272.x: Harakeli Nataka – Vigraharaja IV (Visaladeva) – Inscribed at Adhai Din ka Jhonpra

272.s: At which monument is Vigraharaja IV's play Harakeli Nataka inscribed?
272.x: Harakeli Nataka – Vigraharaja IV (Visaladeva) – Inscribed at Adhai Din ka Jhonpra

272.s: Who wrote the Kirtikaumudi?
272.x: Kirtikaumudi – Someshvara – Vastupala, Vaghela minister

272.s: Which Vaghela minister is praised in the Kirtikaumudi?
272.x: Kirtikaumudi – Someshvara – Vastupala, Vaghela minister

272.s: Who wrote Navasahasanka Charita?
272.x: Navasahasanka Charita – Padmagupta (Parimala) – Paramara Sindhuraja

272.s: Who wrote Hammir Mahakavya?
272.x: Hammir Mahakavya – Nayachandra Suri – Hammir of Ranthambore

272.s: Who wrote the Surajprakash?
272.x: Surajprakash – Karnidan

272.s: What rights did land grants carry in the Rajput feudal structure?
272.x: Feudal structure – Land grants carried revenue, judicial and police rights

272.s: Which historian put forward the theory of "Indian feudalism" with sub-infeudation and forced labour?
272.x: R.S. Sharma's "Indian feudalism" – Sub-infeudation, vishti (forced labour), closed village economy

272.s: What was jauhar?
o: Ritual suicide of a defeated king
272.x: Jauhar – Women's self-immolation to avoid capture (Rani Padmini, Chittor)

272.s: What did Rajput warfare emphasise?
272.x: Warfare: direct, face-to-face combat with emphasis on personal valour; war treated as a sport; clan honour (maan).
